newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly down.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring bids mostly down.

text.p: Spring wheat cash bids were mostly lower on Friday in line with weaker MGE futures.
Dealers cited very little movement amid quiet activity. But concerns lingered regarding potential flooding this spring in the northern Midwest spring wheat-growing region.

Floodwater levels in the Red River valley were forecast to be one to 1-1/2 feet higher than last year's flood based on normal spring weather, Manitoba Natural Resources Minister Glen Cummings said Friday.

"Spring weather conditions will play a critical role in determining the extent and severity of flooding. Precipitation for the month of March has been below average in Manitoba. However, it has been above average in the U.S. portion of the Red River watershed," Cummings said in a statement.

The U.S. portion of the Red River watershed saw three times the average annual snow accumulation this winter while the Canadian side saw twice the average accumulation. There is a 10 percent chance this could be the worst flood of the century, Manitoba Natural Resources has said.
MGE May spring wheat futures lost 5-1/4 cents to end at $4.06-1/4 a bushel, while the rest of the board was five to 8-1/2 cents down.
